title: CedarPark reserved node ops intake
summary: Initial discovery for CedarPark's plan to move inference to Redwood Dedicated. Key themes: need for strict tenant isolation (regulated data), predictable reserved capacity with short bursts of 2-3x baseline, integration with their VPC and corporate SSO/KMS, and a desire to validate tail latency at 99.9th percentile. Next steps: share SSO/KMS security pack, sample SLO/price sheet, and schedule a technical deep dive for benchmarking with a 10k requests/day synthetic load.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, i'll kick off. uh quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Thompson: maya here, head of ML at CedarPark. we're trying to decide between hosted vs reserved nodes, mostly leaning dedicated because of isolation needs.
[00:16] Eric Zhao: eric, platform engineering. i'm the one who will own networking and the VPC peering.
[00:20] Sara Patel: sara, cto. interested in cost predictability and compliance.
[00:25] Jordan Ellis: great, i'm jordan, ae at redwood, and priya (nods) is our solutions eng who will talk through the ops side.
[00:33] Priya Nair: hey all, hi. quick agenda: current stack, spike/burst patterns, security/compliance, and then ops questions (prewarm, failover).
[00:42] Maya Thompson: current stack — we run a mix of gpu nodes on-prem and some inference in GCP. models are Llama2-13B distill and a few small ensembled rerankers. traffic is bursty: baseline ~30 qps, but at product launch we see spikes to 90-100 qps for ~10 minutes. monthly avg tokens about 60M.
[01:05] Priya Nair: ok that helps, so roughly 3x bursts for short windows. do you need hard isolation between tenants?
[01:12] Maya Thompson: yes, we cannot allow co-tenancy with other customers, and we need audit logs per request. so dedicated pools or private deployment.
[01:20] Sara Patel: plus data residency — some pipelines can't leave our VPC.
[01:24] Jordan Ellis: understood. we can do Redwood Dedicated with VPC private endpoints, or Redwood Private for full control. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with isolation and optional tenant fencing; Private gives you the control plane in your VPC.
[01:38] Eric Zhao: what's the difference operationally between tenant fencing and private? like are we still seeing shared infra?
[01:44] Priya Nair: good q. with Dedicated we run reserved nodes for your org only — reserved pools are not shared. we still manage the control plane but we offer VPC peering and private networking. with Private you run the control plane in your network which satisfies strict data residency and air-gap needs. sometimes customers start on Dedicated and move to Private.
[02:02] Maya Thompson: latency SLOs — we care about p50 but especially p99. what do you usually hit for p99 on 13B?
[02:09] Priya Nair: depends on batching and KV cache hit rates. typical p50 is 80-120ms per token on A100-ish hardware with optimized kernels; p99 can be 600-900ms if cold and no prewarm, but with prewarmed hotpool and prefix cache we push p99 down to 200-300ms. there was a weird transcription in our docs that said k v cache which is basically the kv cache for attention.
[02:33] Eric Zhao: ok so prewarm matters. how do you recommend prewarming for short 10-minute spikes vs sustained 2-hour traffic?
[02:41] Priya Nair: prewarm strategy is twofold: maintain a warm pool sized for expected short bursts (a small hotpool of kept-warm model contexts) and autoscale reserved nodes for sustained growth. for 10-minute spikes we suggest a hotpool sized to handle delta; the runtime supports instant warm starts for cached prefixes so if your spikes are predictable we can prewarm on schedule or via webhook.
[03:02] Maya Thompson: can the hotpool be tenant-scoped? we need one tenant's data not to be visible to others.
[03:08] Priya Nair: yes, hotpool is tenant-scoped when using dedicated pools; we pin cache entries to your tenant namespace.
[03:14] Jordan Ellis: are there concerns about cost vs having a larger hotpool?
[03:18] Sara Patel: yes cost. we need to compare unit economics: pay for reserved nodes vs sporadic hosted tokens. we need a sample calc.
[03:25] Jordan Ellis: we'll share an estimate.
[03:27] Eric Zhao: question about fallback — what happens if the reserved pool is saturated?
[03:31] Priya Nair: policy-based routing can fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant or to a smaller quantized model. you can set a strict reject policy too. for enterprise customers we often set a fallback to a smaller low-latency model in another region as a graceful degradation.
[03:48] Maya Thompson: encryption/key mgmt — we use GCP KMS and want customer-managed keys for persisted caches.
[03:55] Priya Nair: we support KMS integrations (GCP, AWS, Azure) and HSM for Private deployments. for Dedicated we can enable envelope encryption with your KMS.
[04:03] Sara Patel: audit logs — we need per-request fields for compliance.
[04:06] Jordan Ellis: redwood provides request-level audit logs, token accounting, and can export to your SIEM via syslog or direct S3 buckets.
[04:16] Eric Zhao: networking — we want private endpoints, no public egress from model infra.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Dedicated supports VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents; for strict no-egress some customers choose Private.
[04:28] Maya Thompson: how long is a typical procurement timeline for Dedicated + VPC?
[04:33] Jordan Ellis: from signature to production we usually see 6-8 weeks for Dedicated with peering and reserved capacity, longer if Private or on-prem.
[04:41] Maya Thompson: ok. do you have SOC 2 or ISO docs we can share with security?
[04:45] Jordan Ellis: yes we'll share our security pack including SOC2, ISO certs, pen test summary, and the KMS/SSO integration guide.
[04:53] Priya Nair: also can run a focused load test for you — we can provision a pilot reserved pool and run a 1-hour synthetic ramp to validate p99 and warmpool behavior.
[05:02] Eric Zhao: that would be helpful. what's the pilot cost or how is it structured?
[05:06] Jordan Ellis: pilots are usually structured as a short-term reserved commit or a timebound trial credits on Dedicated; we'll outline options in the proposal.
[05:14] Maya Thompson: one more: are there hard guarantees on preemption? i.e. if burst demands come from another tenant, will our reserved nodes be preempted?
[05:22] Priya Nair: reserved pools are non-preemptible. only on shared-hosted lanes would you see eviction. but we do offer burst burstable capacity that uses a separate pool which could be preemptible unless you purchase buffer burst blocks.
[05:36] Jordan Ellis: sounds like action items are clear, let's recap.
[05:41] Maya Thompson: agreed.
[05:43] Priya Nair: quick note: we saw some transcript oddities earlier where 'redwood optimize' was transcribed as 'red wood optimum' so ignore small name typos.
[05:54] Jordan Ellis: closing — thanks all, we'll send the security pack, pricing scenarios (3 sizing options), and propose a technical deep dive next week to run bench tests.
[06:04] Sara Patel: thanks, bye.
next_steps: Send security packet (SOC2, ISO, pen test) — Jordan to share by 2025-03-14
Provide 3 reserved sizing/pricing options — Jordan/Priya to send by 2025-03-17
Schedule technical load test deep dive with Priya — target 2025-03-19
Provide sample SLO and p99 benchmarking plan — Priya to include in deep dive
action_items: Jordan Ellis: deliver security pack and pricing scenarios by 2025-03-14/2025-03-17
Priya Nair: prepare benchmarking plan and pilot configuration by 2025-03-17
Eric Zhao: gather VPC network contact and share CIDR ranges by 2025-03-14
Maya Thompson: send model artifact list and token profiles for pilot by 2025-03-15
